newsitem.title: UK: New index to help UK charities measure performance.
newsitem.headline: New index to help UK charities measure performance.

text.p: Britain's leading charities have a new index to let them, and their donors, see how they are performing, its creators Barclays Global Investors and NGO Finance magazine said on Thursday.

"The...Charity 100 index will provide the first serious tool with which charities can measure their performance against the sector as a whole and against indices for other sectors," they said in a statement.
The index, to be published quarterly, charts the performance of the top 100 British charities back to 1992.
They account for about 4.0 billion pounds ($6.49 billion) of the estimated 19 billion pounds ($30.84 billion) in annual income of all Britiain's registered charities.

"It will provide statistical support in charities' dealing with policy makers, government and other funders...(it) will also help the public to understand the importance and progress of the charity sector," the statement added.
The index will be broken down into investment, legacies, other voluntary fundraising, contracts, grants and fees for services, and trading activities.

"Charities are arguably the most under-researched financial institutions in the UK. Up until now nobody has been able to put anything like a sensible figure on their annual income, let alone where this income is coming from," Barclays Global Investors chief executive Andrew Skirton said.
The first results of the index show the charities outstripped inflation but lagged behind the UK share market.
Two critical elements in the increase have been a rise in both investment income and income from grants, fees and charges.
